leads.title: American Samoa Code - marriage provisions
leads.documents: Documents territorial marriage law language referring to age of 'the male' and 'the female' and requiring parties to identify as 'son' and 'daughter', basis for non-licensing of same-sex marriages.
leads.detail: Cited in-text as 'The American Samoa Code does not specify...'; no URL, title number or section number visible in provided text.

leads.title: 1963 sodomy law and 1979 Fono criminal law revision (effective 1980)
leads.documents: Documents criminal status of same-sex sexual activity: 1963 ban on male homosexual and heterosexual sodomy, 1979 revision decriminalizing consensual sodomy except public acts, prostitution, minors or mental incapacity; age of consent 16 regardless of gender/orientation.
leads.detail: Cited in-text with dates 1963, 1979, effective 1980; no URL visible.

leads.title: 2003 bill by Rep. Sua Carl Schuster to ban same-sex marriage
leads.documents: Documents legislative attempt to explicitly ban same-sex marriage to establish territory position and avoid mainland-type lawsuits, and its defeat in House Judiciary Committee and full Senate.
leads.detail: Cited in-text as 2003 legislation by Representative Sua Carl Schuster; no bill number or URL visible.

leads.title: Obergefell v. Hodges (2015)
leads.documents: Documents U.S. Supreme Court same-sex marriage ruling and uncertainty of its application to American Samoa due to U.S. nationals status and unorganized, unincorporated political status.
leads.detail: Cited in-text as 'Obergefell v. Hodges'; no citation or URL visible.

leads.title: Attorney General Talauega Eleasalo Ale - July 2015 review statement
leads.documents: Documents territorial government's official legal position that AG office was 'reviewing the decision to determine its applicability to American Samoa.'
leads.detail: Attributed in-text to Attorney General Talauega Eleasalo Ale, July 2015; no outlet or URL visible.

leads.title: Governor Lolo Matalasi Moliga - 2015 non-applicability statement
leads.documents: Documents executive enforcement stance that Supreme Court ruling does not apply due to preamble, constitution, Christian values and territorial status, backed by Assemblies of God, Catholic Church, and Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
leads.detail: Attributed in-text to Governor Lolo Matalasi Moliga, one week after AG statement; no outlet or URL visible.

leads.title: Respect for Marriage Act (117th U.S. Congress, signed 13 December 2022)
leads.documents: Documents federal requirement that all territories including American Samoa recognize, though not perform, same-sex marriages legally performed elsewhere, with equal treatment of same-sex and opposite-sex couples.
leads.detail: Cited in-text as passed by 117th Congress and signed by President Joe Biden in 2022, effective 13 December 2022; no Public Law number or URL visible.

leads.title: High Court of American Samoa - birth certificate ruling
leads.documents: Documents gender-identity legal status: birth certificates should only be altered to correct information erroneous at recordation or to reflect name change due to adoption, as applied to transgender applicants.
leads.detail: Cited in-text as 'The High Court of American Samoa has held...'; no case name, docket or URL visible.

leads.title: Office of Vital Statistics - interpretation/policy on transgender birth certificates
leads.documents: Documents rights machinery for trans people: will change name with name-change order, and may change gender marker with medical documentation of sex change.
leads.detail: Cited in-text as Office of Vital Statistics interpretation; no regulation number or URL visible.

leads.title: Lambda Legal / ACLU / GLAAD / National Center for Lesbian Rights assistance call and District Court Judge Fiti Alexander Sunia confirmation stance
leads.documents: Documents rights machinery and enforcement: litigation required by denied plaintiffs for recognition, Lambda Legal request for denied couples to contact them, and January 2016 Senate-confirmed judge stating district court does not deal with issue and he would not perform same-sex weddings unless local laws changed.
leads.detail: Cited in-text with expert commentary by Omar Gonzales-Pagan, Chimene Keitner, Prof. Rose Cuison Villazor; no URLs visible.
